findings.note: The host exclusion result is required before the SQLite commit, but the contract does not define its persistence/lease semantics or bind it to task, prior execution, and generation through commit. A host restart or redispatch between exclusion affirmation and the local ownership update could reopen overlap. Specify a durable exclusion/fencing token or equivalent atomic host protocol; SQLite generation checks alone do not close this TOCTOU gap.

The contract requires authenticated provenance and exact scope, while tenant authorization is delegated to the receiving project, but it does not state what tenant/principal context the adapter must bind or validate against task and scope. Define that authorization context and rejection behavior before an adapter can safely serve multi-tenant projects; opaque task IDs and actor labels are not tenant controls.

findings.section: Proposed SQLite ledger and consistency boundary
findings.note: The separate SQLite authority versus state.json/state.md/audit.jsonl boundary is clearly disclaimed, but task bootstrap and the read/write handoff for existing lifecycle progress are not defined. Specify which layer creates/imports task ownership and checkpoints and how status/reporting treats stale projections, so lifecycle views cannot imply a conflicting owner or verified-progress state.
